review: 1:1–1:4 — the Arabic repeats أَتُوقُ ('I long') at the head of the first three lines and then turns to its object; Hebrew repeats אֶשְׁתּוֹקֵק at the same points and keeps the fourth line as the consequence.

2:1–2:2 רְחַץ לִבִּי … הַמַּעְצֵר — Psalm 51:4 (הֶרֶב כַּבְּסֵנִי) and Heb 12:1 (הַמַּעֲמִיסָה); the Arabic اغْسِلِ الْقَلْبَ … يُعِيقُهُ is 'wash the heart of what hinders it', and עָצַר carries 'restrain' without a modern noun.
2:3 שִׁמְעַת נַפְשִׁי — 'my soul's longing', for اشْتِيَاقِي; the noun is built on the same root as the refrain's verb so the stanza stays tied to it.

2:6 תָּאִיר הַלֵּב, כִּי אַתָּה אוֹרוֹ — the Arabic تُنِيرُ الْفُؤَادَ فَأَنْتَ ضِيَاه is 'light the heart, for You are its light'; Hebrew keeps the causal clause but places the pronoun predicate last, as the psalm does in Ps 27:1.
